title: Research Publication: Analysis of VPD Dynamics to Support Precision Irrigation in Open Paddy Fields

body:
**Yogyakarta, December 3, 2025** – **Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada** has produced another research publication in the **Journal of Agricultural and Biosystem Engineering Research (JABER)**. This research analyzes the dynamics of **Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD)** in the microclimate environment of open paddy fields using a **Smart Automatic Weather Station (AWS) of ultrasonic type**.

The cultivation of open paddy fields is strongly influenced by microclimate conditions, such as **air temperature, relative humidity, solar radiation, wind, and rainfall**. Changes in these conditions can affect plant transpiration processes, energy-water balance in the canopy, and plant water requirements. Therefore, microclimate monitoring becomes important to support **data-based precision irrigation systems**.

One important indicator in understanding the relationship between plants and the atmosphere is **Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD)**. Simply put, VPD describes how much "pulling force" the atmosphere exerts on water vapor from the plant. When VPD is high, plants tend to lose more water through transpiration. Conversely, when VPD is low, the atmosphere is more humid and the pressure for water loss from the plant becomes smaller.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/780-1-image-14-728x1030.webp)

The research titled **"Analysis of Vapor Pressure Deficit Dynamics in the Microclimate Environment of Open Paddy Fields Based on Smart Automatic Weather Station of Ultrasonic Type"** was conducted by **Ardan Wiratmoko, Andri Prima Nugroho, Saifuddin Afif, Fahmi Arsyad, Mutiara Alifia Ramadhanty, and Lilik Sutiarso**. The article has been published in **Journal of Agricultural and Biosystem Engineering Research Volume 6 Number 2 Year 2025** on pages **118–136**.

The research was conducted on open paddy fields around **Balai Penyuluhan Pertanian Wates, Kulon Progo Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta**. Microclimate observations were conducted during **December 3–11, 2024** using a **Smart Automatic Weather Station of ultrasonic type** capable of automatically and periodically recording environmental data.

The AWS system used recorded various microclimate parameters, such as **air temperature, relative humidity, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, rainfall, and solar light intensity**. Data were recorded at **10-minute intervals**, thus providing a more detailed picture of microclimate changes throughout the day.

Simply put, this research not only examined weather conditions in general, but also analyzed how **temperature and humidity shape VPD values** over time. The collected data were then analyzed using a **Python**-based computational approach, including statistical analysis, correlation analysis, heatmap visualization, and **VPD clustering** to group atmospheric conditions into operational categories.

The research results showed that the environment of open paddy fields during the observation period had relatively humid microclimate conditions. The average air temperature was recorded at **27.19 °C**, average relative humidity was **88.81%**, and average VPD value was **0.46 kPa** with a range of **0.01–1.79 kPa**. This value indicates that the atmospheric conditions were dominated by low to moderate vapor pressure deficits.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/780-2-image-15-1030x355.webp)

Correlation analysis showed that VPD was strongly influenced by **air temperature** and **relative humidity**. VPD had a very strong positive correlation with air temperature, approximately **r ≈ 0.96**, and a very strong negative correlation with relative humidity, approximately **r ≈ −1.00**. This indicates that VPD increases when temperature rises and humidity decreases, particularly during the daytime period when solar radiation reaches its peak.

Daily visualization showed that VPD values tended to be low from **night to early morning**, when air temperature was lower and humidity approached saturation. Conversely, VPD increased from **morning to afternoon**, particularly around the period **08.00–14.00 WIB**, when air temperature increased and relative humidity decreased. This period is important because it is potentially related to increased plant water requirements.

Through the **clustering approach**, VPD conditions were grouped into three categories, namely **low vapor deficit, moderate vapor deficit, and high vapor deficit**. Clustering results showed that **low vapor deficit conditions** were dominant with a percentage of **53.67%**, followed by **high vapor deficit at 28.32%**, and **moderate vapor deficit at 18.01%**. This result indicates that although the paddy environment tends to be humid, there remain periods with high atmospheric pressure that need to be considered in water management.

## **Collaboration and Support:**

This research was conducted by a team from **Smart Agriculture Research Center, Department of Agricultural Engineering and Biosystems, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada**. Collaboration within this team brought together expertise in the fields of **precision agriculture, agricultural microclimate, sensor systems, automatic weather stations, data analysis, and irrigation water management**.

Through this collaboration, the research not only focused on weather measurement, but also connected microclimate data with practical needs in open paddy field cultivation. This approach is important because information on temperature, humidity, radiation, and VPD can be used as a basis for understanding periods of critical plant water requirements in a more objective manner.

The research team expresses gratitude to **PUAPT UGM (Center of Excellence for Inter-University Collaboration Universitas Gadjah Mada)** for the facility support so that this research could be implemented. The research team also expresses appreciation to the **Smart Agriculture Research Center, Department of Agricultural Engineering and Biosystems, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada**, for technical assistance and support throughout the system development, research implementation, data collection, and analysis stages.

## **Benefits and Impact:**

This research provides important contribution to the development of **data-based microclimate monitoring systems** in open paddy field cultivation. By understanding VPD dynamics, farmers, researchers, and irrigation managers can obtain better information regarding periods when plants are likely to experience increased water requirements.

VPD information can help support **precision irrigation**, particularly in determining when atmospheric conditions drive plants to lose more water through transpiration. Thus, water management can be directed to be more responsive to actual environmental conditions, rather than based only on fixed schedules.

This approach is also beneficial for supporting **mitigation of atmospheric stress** on rice plants. When the system detects periods of high VPD, land managers can be more alert to the possibility of increased water requirements, especially during growth phases that are sensitive to water shortage.

From the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** perspective, this research supports **SDG 2: Zero Hunger** because it contributes to the development of technology to support productivity and resilience of rice production systems. This research is also aligned with **SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation** through the potential for more efficient irrigation water management. Additionally, the use of **Smart Automatic Weather Station, microclimate sensors, data analysis, and VPD clustering** supports **SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure** through the development of smart agricultural technology innovation. In the long term, this technology also supports **SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production** and **SDG 13: Climate Action**, because it helps promote rice cultivation that is more adaptive to climate dynamics and more efficient in water resource use.

In the future, this approach has the potential to be further developed with the integration of **Internet of Things (IoT), microclimate monitoring dashboard, high VPD early warning system, and data-based irrigation recommendations**. This integration can strengthen the implementation of **smart farming** in open paddy field cultivation, particularly in addressing climate change and daily weather variability.

**The full publication of this research can be accessed through the following DOI link:** [http://dx.doi.org/10.20884/1.jaber.2025.6.2.19697](http://dx.doi.org/10.20884/1.jaber.2025.6.2.19697)

**Contact:** Ardan Wiratmoko, S.T.P., M.Sc. ardan.w@ugm.ac.id

original.body:
**Yogyakarta, 3 Desember 2025** – **Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada** kembali menghasilkan publikasi penelitian di **Journal of Agricultural and Biosystem Engineering Research (JABER)**. Penelitian ini menganalisis dinamika **Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD)** pada lingkungan mikroklimat padi sawah terbuka menggunakan **Smart Automatic Weather Station (AWS) tipe ultrasonik**.

Budidaya padi sawah terbuka sangat dipengaruhi oleh kondisi mikroklimat, seperti **suhu udara, kelembaban relatif, radiasi matahari, angin, dan curah hujan**. Perubahan kondisi tersebut dapat memengaruhi proses transpirasi tanaman, keseimbangan energi-air pada kanopi, serta kebutuhan air tanaman. Oleh karena itu, pemantauan mikroklimat menjadi penting untuk mendukung sistem **irigasi presisi berbasis data**.

Salah satu indikator penting dalam memahami hubungan antara tanaman dan atmosfer adalah **Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD)**. Secara sederhana, VPD menggambarkan seberapa besar “daya tarik” atmosfer terhadap uap air dari tanaman. Ketika VPD tinggi, tanaman cenderung kehilangan lebih banyak air melalui transpirasi. Sebaliknya, ketika VPD rendah, atmosfer lebih lembap dan tekanan kehilangan air dari tanaman menjadi lebih kecil.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/780-1-image-14-728x1030.webp)

Penelitian yang berjudul **“Analisis Dinamika Vapor Pressure Deficit pada Lingkungan Mikroklimat Padi Sawah Terbuka Berbasis Smart Automatic Weather Station Tipe Ultrasonik”** ini dilakukan oleh **Ardan Wiratmoko, Andri Prima Nugroho, Saifuddin Afif, Fahmi Arsyad, Mutiara Alifia Ramadhanty, dan Lilik Sutiarso**. Artikel ini telah dipublikasikan dalam **Journal of Agricultural and Biosystem Engineering Research Volume 6 Nomor 2 Tahun 2025** pada halaman **118–136**.

Penelitian dilakukan pada lahan padi sawah terbuka di sekitar **Balai Penyuluhan Pertanian Wates, Kabupaten Kulon Progo, Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta**. Pengamatan mikroklimat dilakukan selama **3–11 Desember 2024** menggunakan **Smart Automatic Weather Station tipe ultrasonik** yang mampu mencatat data lingkungan secara otomatis dan berkala.

Sistem AWS yang digunakan mencatat berbagai parameter mikroklimat, seperti **suhu udara, kelembaban relatif, tekanan udara, kecepatan angin, arah angin, curah hujan, dan intensitas cahaya matahari**. Data direkam dengan interval **10 menit**, sehingga mampu memberikan gambaran perubahan mikroklimat secara lebih detail sepanjang hari.

Secara sederhana, penelitian ini tidak hanya melihat kondisi cuaca secara umum, tetapi juga menganalisis bagaimana **suhu dan kelembaban membentuk nilai VPD** dari waktu ke waktu. Data yang terkumpul kemudian dianalisis menggunakan pendekatan komputasional berbasis **Python**, termasuk analisis statistik, korelasi, visualisasi heatmap, dan **clustering VPD** untuk mengelompokkan kondisi atmosfer menjadi kategori operasional.

Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa lingkungan padi sawah terbuka selama periode pengamatan memiliki kondisi mikroklimat yang relatif lembap. Suhu udara rata-rata tercatat sebesar **27,19 °C**, kelembaban relatif rata-rata sebesar **88,81%**, dan nilai VPD rata-rata sebesar **0,46 kPa** dengan rentang **0,01–1,79 kPa**. Nilai ini menunjukkan bahwa kondisi atmosfer didominasi oleh defisit tekanan uap rendah hingga sedang.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/780-2-image-15-1030x355.webp)

Analisis korelasi menunjukkan bahwa VPD sangat dipengaruhi oleh **suhu udara** dan **kelembaban relatif**. VPD memiliki korelasi positif yang sangat kuat dengan suhu udara, yaitu sekitar **r ≈ 0,96**, dan korelasi negatif yang sangat kuat dengan kelembaban relatif, yaitu sekitar **r ≈ −1,00**. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa VPD meningkat ketika suhu naik dan kelembaban menurun, terutama pada periode siang hari ketika radiasi matahari mencapai puncaknya.

Visualisasi harian menunjukkan bahwa nilai VPD cenderung rendah pada **malam hingga dini hari**, ketika suhu udara lebih rendah dan kelembaban mendekati jenuh. Sebaliknya, VPD meningkat pada **pagi hingga siang hari**, terutama sekitar periode **08.00–14.00 WIB**, ketika suhu udara meningkat dan kelembaban relatif menurun. Periode ini menjadi penting karena berpotensi berkaitan dengan peningkatan kebutuhan air tanaman.

Melalui pendekatan **clustering**, kondisi VPD dikelompokkan menjadi tiga kategori, yaitu **defisit uap rendah, defisit uap sedang, dan defisit uap tinggi**. Hasil clustering menunjukkan bahwa kondisi **defisit uap rendah** mendominasi dengan persentase **53,67%**, diikuti oleh **defisit uap tinggi sebesar 28,32%**, dan **defisit uap sedang sebesar 18,01%**. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa meskipun lingkungan sawah cenderung lembap, tetap terdapat periode dengan tekanan atmosfer tinggi yang perlu diperhatikan dalam pengelolaan air.

## **Kolaborasi dan Dukungan:**

Penelitian ini dilaksanakan oleh tim dari **Smart Agriculture Research Center, Departemen Teknik Pertanian dan Biosistem, Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian, Universitas Gadjah Mada**. Kolaborasi dalam tim ini mempertemukan keahlian dalam bidang **pertanian presisi, mikroklimat pertanian, sistem sensor, automatic weather station, analisis data, dan manajemen air irigasi**.

Melalui kolaborasi tersebut, penelitian ini tidak hanya berfokus pada pengukuran cuaca, tetapi juga menghubungkan data mikroklimat dengan kebutuhan praktis dalam budidaya padi sawah terbuka. Pendekatan ini penting karena informasi suhu, kelembaban, radiasi, dan VPD dapat digunakan sebagai dasar untuk memahami periode kritis kebutuhan air tanaman secara lebih objektif.

Tim peneliti menyampaikan terima kasih kepada **PUAPT UGM (Pusat Unggulan Antar Perguruan Tinggi Universitas Gadjah Mada)** atas dukungan fasilitas sehingga penelitian ini dapat dilaksanakan. Tim peneliti juga menyampaikan apresiasi kepada **Smart Agriculture Research Center, Departemen Teknik Pertanian dan Biosistem, Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian, Universitas Gadjah Mada**, atas bantuan teknis dan dukungan selama proses pengembangan sistem, pelaksanaan penelitian, pengumpulan data, hingga tahap analisis.

## **Manfaat dan Dampak:**

Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi penting bagi pengembangan **sistem pemantauan mikroklimat berbasis data** pada budidaya padi sawah terbuka. Dengan memahami dinamika VPD, petani, peneliti, dan pengelola irigasi dapat memperoleh informasi yang lebih baik mengenai periode ketika tanaman berpotensi mengalami peningkatan kebutuhan air.

Informasi VPD dapat membantu mendukung **irigasi presisi**, terutama dalam menentukan kapan kondisi atmosfer mendorong tanaman untuk kehilangan air lebih banyak melalui transpirasi. Dengan demikian, pengelolaan air dapat diarahkan agar lebih responsif terhadap kondisi aktual lingkungan, bukan hanya berdasarkan jadwal tetap.

Pendekatan ini juga bermanfaat untuk mendukung **mitigasi stres atmosfer** pada tanaman padi. Ketika sistem mendeteksi periode VPD tinggi, pengelola lahan dapat lebih waspada terhadap kemungkinan peningkatan kebutuhan air, terutama pada fase pertumbuhan yang sensitif terhadap kekurangan air.

Dari sisi **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, penelitian ini mendukung **SDG 2: Zero Hunger** karena berkontribusi pada pengembangan teknologi untuk mendukung produktivitas dan ketahanan sistem produksi padi. Penelitian ini juga sejalan dengan **SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation** melalui potensi pengelolaan air irigasi yang lebih efisien. Selain itu, penggunaan **Smart Automatic Weather Station, sensor mikroklimat, analisis data, dan clustering VPD** mendukung **SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure** melalui pengembangan inovasi teknologi pertanian cerdas. Dalam jangka panjang, teknologi ini juga mendukung **SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production** dan **SDG 13: Climate Action**, karena membantu mendorong budidaya padi yang lebih adaptif terhadap dinamika iklim dan lebih efisien dalam penggunaan sumber daya air.

Ke depan, pendekatan ini berpotensi dikembangkan lebih lanjut dengan integrasi **Internet of Things (IoT), dashboard monitoring mikroklimat, sistem peringatan dini VPD tinggi, dan rekomendasi irigasi berbasis data**. Integrasi tersebut dapat memperkuat penerapan **smart farming** pada budidaya padi sawah terbuka, khususnya dalam menghadapi perubahan iklim dan variabilitas cuaca harian.

**Publikasi lengkap penelitian ini dapat diakses melalui tautan DOI berikut:**[http://dx.doi.org/10.20884/1.jaber.2025.6.2.19697](http://dx.doi.org/10.20884/1.jaber.2025.6.2.19697)
